title: Multi-Game Collection Architecture
description:
# Multi-Game Collection Architecture

## Problem Statement

Pixi Square is currently a single-game monolith focused on the grid-world gameplay. The codebase is organized around one game instance, one set of scenes, and one set of ECS systems. To scale this into a collection of diverse games, we need:

- Clean separation between games (no event crosstalk, isolated Phaser instances)
- A game registry that can be extended without modifying routing or startup logic
- Each game to own its own scenes, systems, and UI components
- Preservation of the existing Vue/Phaser boundary and testability

## Solution

Refactor the project into a **multi-game collection framework** where:

1. **Shared Infrastructure** (`shared/`) contains common systems, utilities (EventBus, StartGame factories), and reusable Vue components
2. **Games** (`games/{gameId}/`) are self-contained folders with their own scenes, systems, components, and entry point
3. **Game Manifests** declare metadata (title, thumbnail, scenes) for dynamic discovery
4. **Dynamic Routing** registers routes at app startup based on loaded manifests
5. **Game-scoped Stores** (Pinia) track `currentScene` per game instance without cross-game interference
6. **Per-game Phaser Instances** are created on route mount and destroyed on unmount

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want to add a new game to the collection without modifying router or startup code, so that I can grow the game library independently
2. As a developer, I want each game to have its own EventBus instance, so that events in one game don't trigger listeners in another
3. As a developer, I want to share common ECS systems between games, so that I don't duplicate pathfinding, physics, or other infrastructure
4. As a player, I want to see a menu with tiles for each available game, so that I can choose which game to play
5. As a player, I want to navigate between the menu and individual games smoothly, so that switching games feels natural
6. As a player, I want each game to have independent scene transitions (MainMenu → Gameplay → GameOver), so that one game's flow doesn't interfere with another's
7. As a developer, I want each game's scenes and systems to be in a dedicated folder, so that the codebase remains navigable as more games are added
8. As a developer, I want the Vue/Phaser boundary to remain intact across all games, so that game logic stays testable and game scenes stay Vue-free
9. As a developer, I want to test game registries, manifests, and scene initialization independently, so that I can validate the multi-game architecture
10. As a player, I want the game menu to load at app startup and show all available games, so that I can see my options immediately

## Implementation Decisions

### Directory Structure

```
src/
├── shared/                           # Shared game infrastructure (Vue-free except components/views)
│   ├── systems/                      # ECS systems available to all games
│   │   ├── MovementSystem.ts
│   │   ├── WandererAISystem.ts
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── utils/                        # Shared utilities (Vue-free)
│   │   ├── EventBus.ts              # Factory: creates new EventBus per game
│   │   ├── StartGame.ts             # Factory: initializes Phaser with scenes + EventBus
│   │   ├── games-registry.ts        # Loader: discovers all game manifests
│   │   └── ...common utilities...
│   ├── components/                   # Reusable Vue components
│   │   ├── GameTile.vue             # Tile component for game selector
│   │   └── ...
│   └── views/                        # Reusable Vue views
│       ├── AppLayout.vue            # Root layout: canvas + overlay
│       ├── MenuView.vue             # Game selector menu
│       ├── SettingsView.vue
│       └── ...
│
├── games/                            # Game collection
│   ├── grid-world/                   # Example game
│   │   ├── index.ts                 # Exports manifest + StartGame factory
│   │   ├── manifest.ts              # Metadata: { id, title, thumbnail, sceneNames, startScene }
│   │   ├── scenes/
│   │   │   ├── Boot.ts
│   │   │   ├── Preloader.ts
│   │   │   ├── MainMenu.ts
│   │   │   ├── GameScene.ts
│   │   │   ├── HUDScene.ts
│   │   │   └── GameOverScene.ts
│   │   ├── systems/                 # Grid-world specific systems
│   │   │   ├── WandererAISystem.ts
│   │   │   └── ...
│   │   ├── utils/                   # Grid-world specific utilities
│   │   │   ├── gridPathfinding.ts
│   │   │   └── ...
│   │   ├── components/              # Grid-world specific Vue components
│   │   │   └── ...
│   │   └── views/
│   │       └── GameView.vue         # Entry point: mounts Phaser instance
│   │
│   ├── puzzle-game/                  # Future game (follows same pattern)
│   │   ├── index.ts
│   │   ├── manifest.ts
│   │   ├── scenes/
│   │   ├── systems/
│   │   ├── utils/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   └── views/
│   │       └── GameView.vue
│   │
│   └── games-registry.ts             # Central: imports all manifests + builds registry
│
├── router/
│   └── index.ts                      # Dynamically registers game routes at startup
│
├── stores/
│   ├── games-registry.ts             # Pinia: loads registry, manages route registration
│   └── current-game.ts               # Pinia (game-scoped): currentScene, eventBus
│
├── App.vue
└── main.ts
```

### Key Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|-----------------|
| `shared/utils/EventBus.ts` | Factory: creates new `Phaser.Events.EventEmitter` per game instance |
| `shared/utils/StartGame.ts` | Factory: accepts `(parent, gameId, manifest, eventBus)`, initializes Phaser with scenes |
| `shared/utils/games-registry.ts` | Loader: imports all game `index.ts` files, collects manifests, returns registry array |
| `games/{gameId}/manifest.ts` | Metadata: `{ id, title, thumbnail, sceneNames[], startScene }` |
| `games/{gameId}/views/GameView.vue` | Entry point: receives `:gameId` param, creates Phaser instance, owns game store |
| `stores/games-registry.ts` | Pinia: bootstraps registry at app startup, registers dynamic routes |
| `stores/current-game.ts` | Pinia (game-scoped): tracks `currentScene` string, updates from EventBus |
| `router/index.ts` | Registers static routes (menu, settings) + dynamic game routes after registry loads |

### Manifest Schema

```ts
export interface GameManifest {
  id: string                      // 'grid-world', 'puzzle-game', etc.
  title: string                   // Display name
  thumbnail: string               // Asset path or URL
  sceneNames: string[]            // ['Boot', 'Preloader', 'MainMenu', 'GameScene', 'GameOver']
  startScene: string              // Which scene to boot first: 'MainMenu'
}
```

### Game Instance Lifecycle

1. Router navigates to `#/{gameId}` (e.g., `#/grid-world`)
2. `{Game}GameView.vue` mounts, receives `gameId` as route param
3. GameView looks up manifest in registry
4. GameView creates new Phaser `Game` instance (not reactive, not in `ref()`)
5. GameView creates game-scoped Pinia store (currentScene, eventBus)
6. StartGame factory boots the `startScene` (e.g., MainMenu)
7. Game runs: scene transitions happen inside Phaser, trigger EventBus events
8. EventBus events update Vue store's `currentScene`
9. Vue conditionally renders UI based on `currentScene`
10. Player navigates away → GameView unmounts → Phaser instance destroyed

### Vue/Phaser Boundary

**`shared/` is Vue-free except `components/` and `views/`:**
- ✅ `shared/systems/`, `shared/utils/` — no Vue imports
- ✅ `shared/components/`, `shared/views/` — Vue components OK
- ❌ Game logic in `games/{gameId}/` — no Vue imports (except views/)

**Each game's entry point:**
- `games/{gameId}/views/GameView.vue` — sole importer of `shared/utils/StartGame`
- Calls `StartGame(parent, gameId, manifest, eventBus)` to create game instance
- Owns the returned Phaser instance (never in reactive container)

### Event Communication

**EventBus per game (no cross-game leakage):**
```ts
// In shared/utils/EventBus.ts
export function createGameEventBus(): Phaser.Events.EventEmitter {
  return new Phaser.Events.EventEmitter()
}

// In games/{gameId}/views/GameView.vue
const eventBus = createGameEventBus()
StartGame(parent, gameId, manifest, eventBus)
```

**Scenes emit scene-change events:**
```ts
// In games/{gameId}/scenes/MainMenu.ts
this.scene.start('GameScene', {}, true) // isVisible = true
eventBus.emit('scene:start', { name: 'GameScene' })
```

**Vue listens and updates store:**
```ts
// In stores/current-game.ts (Pinia)
eventBus.on('scene:start', ({ name }) => {
  currentScene.value = name
})
```

### Dynamic Route Registration

**At app startup** (in `main.ts` or app-init store):
```ts
import { gamesRegistry } from '@/games/games-registry'

const store = useGamesRegistryStore()
await store.loadRegistry() // collects all manifests
store.registerGameRoutes() // adds /:gameId → {Game}GameView routes
```

**Router configuration:**
```ts
// Existing static routes
{ path: '/', component: MenuView },
{ path: '/settings', component: SettingsView },

// Dynamic routes (registered after registry loads)
{ path: '/:gameId', component: resolveGameView(gameId) }
```

## Testing Decisions

### What Makes a Good Test
- Test **external behavior**, not implementation details
- Mock boundaries (EventBus, Phaser instance) at the entry point
- Test **integration** between registry, routes, and game startup
- Avoid tightly coupling tests to scene names or file paths

### Modules to Test

| Module | Test Focus |
|--------|-----------|
| `games-registry.ts` loader | Manifest discovery, registry shape, missing manifests |
| Manifest validation | Schema conformance (id, title, thumbnail, sceneNames, startScene required) |
| `StartGame` factory | Phaser instance creation, scene initialization, EventBus passed through |
| Game-scoped Pinia store | `currentScene` updates from EventBus events |
| Route registration | Dynamic routes created for each game, correct components resolved |
| `GameView.vue` component (per game) | Mounts Phaser, passes EventBus, unmounts cleanly |

### Prior Art
- Current codebase tests mock EventBus with `vi.mock('@/game/EventBus', ...)`
- Use same pattern for game-scoped stores and StartGame factory
- Integration tests can spin up a real registry and validate route registration

## Out of Scope

- **Game-to-game state persistence** — each game instance is independent; no cross-game save files or shared progress
- **Asset sharing between games** — each game bundles its own textures, audio, tilemaps
- **Code splitting / lazy loading** — all games are loaded at app startup (can be added later)
- **Analytics / telemetry** — tracking which games are played, playtime, etc.
- **Multiplayer between games** — local multiplayer (P1/P2) stays within a single game
- **Game progression / skill trees** — global progression systems across games are out of scope

## Further Notes

1. **Migration Path**: Grid-World is the first game; it becomes `games/grid-world/`. The refactor preserves all existing gameplay logic — only the folder structure and entry point change.

2. **Extensibility**: Adding a new game requires:
   - New folder `games/{gameId}/`
   - Manifest export in `games/{gameId}/manifest.ts`
   - Index export in `games/{gameId}/index.ts`
   - Single line in `games/games-registry.ts` to import the new manifest

3. **DevX**: Each game is fully isolated; developers can work on one game without touching others or the shared infrastructure.

4. **Testing**: The registry, manifest, and route registration are all testable in isolation. Game-specific scene logic remains behind the EventBus boundary.
